key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects and disordered regions in TiAl, where it pins dislocations and suppresses deformation twinning to strengthen the alloy at high temperature.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect structure could improve TiAl’s high-temperature strength, while brittle borides and termination-dependent interface adhesion require attention.
method: Develop a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Use hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics to study boron redistribution.
Analyze deformation, defect interactions, and stacking-fault energetics.
evidence_signal: Polycrystalline TiAl simulations show a 9.4% increase in average flow stress at 1 at.% boron and 900 K, accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The reported strengthening is simulation-based; experimental validation and transferability across processing conditions remain to be established.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
